items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: I'd go to see Clarence Whitman... Clarence gave us plenty of work. That time he'd done several recordings a week... I made records... everyone, even the Edison at that time... we made a watchful records for everybody.

ctx.x: Well I was with the show, I was traveling with the show. Oh I see. That was after you went back to St. Louis you got with the show.

No, after I went back to St. Louis, I worked in a night club there called Show for the Garden, for about, oh let's see, it was about a year or so. I was just getting up near 26 or 27, I was about to say about 25 when I was at St. Louis. I went to Chicago, someone called me to come to Chicago, to work at the night club there called the, after Oswald, I don't remember the real name of it, but that was the first time I ever met Earl Hines. He was there, had a band there five, six people, a friend of mine from St.…
The songs that Clarence Williams recorded were mostly his own songs?
